quota/kubernetes/ResourceQuota.CheckRequ.note: Refuted by a status write: CheckRequest skips the hard-limit check for the status subresource (controller.go:614, added in commit 27706a0b 'Add quota support for PVC with VolumeAttributesClass') and still adds the usage, so used can pass hard. The original does it (repro: a status create with usage r0=1 against hard r0=0 is admitted with used r0=1; the same request without the subresource is refused). By design: a status write reports what was already admitted. The law is removed; the corpus keeps 'an admitted request leaves every resource it charges within its hard limit', the same claim for every request but status writes.
The restated intent of the refuted 'every admitted request leaves the usage it charges within the hard limits': the check holds for every request but status writes. Proven.

quota/litellm/maxBudgetChecks#a team who.note: Suspected real bug (an inconsistency, low severity). team_max_budget_check (auth_checks.py:6386) refuses only at spend > max_budget, so a team whose spend equals its max_budget is admitted, while the key (:5912), user, org and window checks refuse at spend >= max_budget. The original does it (repro: key at spend 1.0 of 1.0 refused, team at 1.0 of 1.0 admitted). The repo's own tests/e2e/quota_management/budgets/BUDGET_CODE_MATRIX.md:38-39 lists it under 'flags from the code' as 'Comparison operators are inconsistent ... Spend exactly at max_budget blocks a key but not a team', not as an intent. Law and rule kept; no issue opened.

quota/litellm/maxBudgetChecks#a key's sp.note: Refuted by requests admitted while others are in flight: each read-time check reads the spend counter before any response's cost is added, so n overlapping requests overshoot by n costs. The original does it (repro: two requests at spend 0.9 of 1.0 both admitted, 1.9 after both charges). The read-time check is not meant to bound concurrent overspend: LiteLLM's pre-call reservation (budget_reservation.py, its 'concurrent-overspend protection') is. Restated as 'while requests do not overlap, a key's spend passes its max_budget by at most one request's cost' (an overlap ghost in the rule).

quota/litellm/maxBudgetChecks#while requ.note: The restated law (see the original's entry). Unknown at 3 s locally: it needs 'no overlap implies at most one in flight, admitted below the budget', which the search did not find.
